candidates.name: vrbo-scraper (Edioff)
candidates.what_it_holds: Python 3.10+ Selenium/undetected-chromedriver scraper: discovers Vrbo listings by city search then visits each property page to extract 30+ fields (property info, pricing, lat/lon, room config, amenities, host details, cancellation policy, up to 12 image URLs) into timestamped JSON under data/. Includes cities.vrbo.json config listing target cities/search params. MIT license, only 2 commits, 0 stars - very young/unproven, includes captcha-detection-with-manual-prompt (i.e. not fully automatable).
candidates.why_useful: Directly targets gap #9 (Vrbo/HomeAway competitor supply) with a field schema (price, amenities, host) close to what would be needed to build a Vrbo supply/price panel comparable to Inside Airbnb; would need to actually be run and maintained over time to be useful (a one-time pull is not point-in-time series).

candidates.name: web-crawler-with-proxies
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed Vrbo.com crawler (105 commits) using Crawlera API + Hotspot Shield VPN proxy rotation against vrbo.com/search/keywords:<LOCATION>/page:<PAGE_NUM> to pull city-level listing routes/IDs and prices, writing city-price pairs to parsed_data.txt plus CDF price-distribution plots per city. No committed data files (locations_to_crawl.txt is an empty template); requires paid proxy/VPN services to run.
candidates.why_useful: A second working method for pulling Vrbo prices by city (gap #9, and adjacent to gap #2 realised ADR-type data), with more mature crawling infra (105 commits) than most Vrbo scrapers found, though it needs paid proxies and produces no historical snapshot on its own.

candidates.name: booking-sites-parser
candidates.what_it_holds: Apache-2.0 Python CLI parser (28 commits, 3 stars) for Booking.com, Homeaway.com and Airbnb.com listing pages; installable as `booking-sites-parser` package, run via `python -m booking_sites_parser <url>`. No data fields documented in README beyond usage examples; no data files committed; has a /tests directory.
candidates.why_useful: One tool covering three relevant platforms (Homeaway + Booking.com + Airbnb) in one schema, which would ease cross-platform supply comparisons under gap #9 if it still works against current site markup (unclear given age/inactivity).

candidates.name: vrbo-main-link-scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Commercial-flavored ("Bitbash") lightweight Vrbo link/ID extractor outputting JSON {listing_url, property_id, location, title, scraped_at}; claims 1,200 links/minute, 98%+ success. Single commit, no license specified, 0 stars, sample JSON in README only (one record).
candidates.why_useful: Only gives listing IDs/URLs, not price/amenity data - a discovery step, not a supply/price panel by itself. Low value unless paired with a detail scraper like Edioff/vrbo-scraper.

candidates.name: mcp-vrbo
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server letting an AI agent book/search Vrbo vacation rentals; found via github.com/topics/vrbo listing. Not independently verified in depth (budget-constrained) - appears to be an agent-tooling wrapper, likely around a paid or scraped backend, not a data store.
candidates.why_useful: Possible live-query method for current Vrbo pricing/availability if it works without paid keys, but role is agent tooling, not a dataset; would need a follow-up fetch to confirm backend and licensing.

candidates.name: vrbo-api (StayingAPI)
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed REST + native MCP wrapper claiming live Vrbo (plus Airbnb, Booking.com, Google Hotels) search, availability calendars, and pricing in one normalized schema. Free tier via sandbox key (stay_test_ prefix, deterministic mock data); production keys need signup but 'no credit card', and 'failed/empty/blocked calls are never billed'. Only 3 commits; third-party (not an official Vrbo product - Vrbo itself has no public self-serve API). Also topic-tagged as vrbo-api, last topic update 21 Jul 2026 (recently active).
candidates.why_useful: If the free tier genuinely returns live Vrbo pricing/availability without a paid key, this is a real one-command pull for point-in-time Vrbo pricing snapshots (gap #9 and could contribute to gap #2 realised-ADR type data) - but it is a commercial third-party reseller of unclear reliability/ToS status for repeated pulls; would need hands-on testing (out of scope for this cataloguing pass) and a ToS check before use.

candidates.name: property-occupancy
candidates.what_it_holds: MIT-licensed TypeScript/npm package (11 commits, 3 stars) computing daily/monthly occupancy-rate percentages from a caller-supplied array of reservation {check-in, check-out} objects; mentions Airbnb/Booking.com/VRBO as target platforms but does not itself pull or integrate any listing/reservation data.
candidates.why_useful: Pure calculation utility, not a data source - would only be useful if paired with an actual VRBO reservation feed, which the team does not have. Cataloguing for completeness only.

candidates.name: rapid-java-sdk
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Expedia Group open-source Kotlin/Java SDK (Apache-2.0) for the Rapid API (formerly EPS - Expedia Partner Solutions), which since Expedia's platform unification exposes lodging supply/rates across Expedia's Brand Expedia, Hotels.com, Vrbo and other properties through one partner API. This is a client library, not data; Rapid API access requires an Expedia Partner Solutions/affiliate contract and API key (not free/self-serve), so it is a documented pull method only if the team can obtain partner credentials.
candidates.why_useful: The most authoritative possible pointer to Expedia Group's actual vacation-rental (Vrbo) supply/pricing feed (gap #9), directly from Expedia Group's own GitHub org - but practically gated behind a partner agreement, so not usable without a business relationship the team likely does not have.

candidates.name: short-term-rentals-warehouse
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Inside Airbnb (already held, 13-city panel + broader cohorts)
candidates.what_it_holds: Snowflake/DBT/Metabase data warehouse (15 stars, 68 commits) combining Inside Airbnb listings (2015-2020, 35M+ records across world cities) with Kaggle 'World Cities Population and Location' and Kaggle 'Cost of Living Indices' (Numbeo-sourced) for an Airbnb-housing-impact analysis. Confirmed no Vrbo/HomeAway data despite appearing under the vacation-rental/short-term-rental topic search.
candidates.why_useful: Not new data (Airbnb-only, and our Inside Airbnb holdings already run 2022-2026) but the DBT pipeline pattern plus the two Kaggle joins (world-city population, cost-of-living index) could be reusable methodology for normalizing/joining STR panels to macro city context.

candidates.name: channex-mcp
candidates.what_it_holds: MCP server wrapping the Channex channel-manager API (properties, room_types, rate_plans) which syncs inventory/rates across many OTAs including Vrbo, Booking.com and Airbnb for property managers. Found via github.com/topics/short-term-rental (5 stars); not independently verified in depth.
candidates.why_useful: A channel-manager-side integration point that could in principle expose cross-platform (including Vrbo) rate-plan data if the operator has a Channex account, but this is host-side tooling requiring the team to control listings - not a public dataset.

notes: Hard blocker this run: the shared WebSearch tool budget for the session was already exhausted (200/200) before my first query executed - almost certainly consumed by other concurrently-running scout agents sharing this session/account, since my own theme had not searched yet. I pivoted entirely to WebFetch against static pages: (1) github.com/search?q=... repo-search endpoint worked for exactly two queries before returning HTTP 429 with Retry-After 3600 (one-hour block, again presumably shared quota with concurrent scouts hitting github.com from the same egress IP); (2) Bing, Google, DuckDuckGo (HTML and lite), Mojeek, Startpage, sourcegraph.com and grep.app were all either bot-blocked (403/429/CAPTCHA) or returned useless brand-name-only results via the WebFetch markdown summarizer (Bing repeatedly returned vrbo.com/GitHub-homepage results regardless of query terms - the summarizing sub-fetch appears to not honor '+github.com' or 'site:' operators well for non-trivial queries); (3) github.com/topics/<tag> pages were NOT rate-limited and became the main working discovery channel - I pulled vrbo, homeaway, vacation-rental, expedia, short-term-rental, vrbo-api and vrbo-scraper topic pages, then verified ~10 individual repo pages directly (these plain repo-page fetches also stayed under the rate limit). Bottom line for this theme: there is NO committed Vrbo/HomeAway dataset (CSV/JSON dump, release asset, or academic replication package) on GitHub that I could find - every relevant repo is either a scraper/crawler with no committed historical data, a paid/freemium third-party API wrapper, a UI clone/prototype with fake seed data, or Expedia Group's own official but partner-gated Rapid API SDK. This matches the general pattern noted elsewhere in the sweep that Vrbo/HomeAway, unlike Airbnb, has no equivalent of an 'Inside Airbnb' community data-dump project - nobody appears to have built and open-sourced a recurring Vrbo listings/calendar scrape at any meaningful scale. If this gap matters enough to the pitch, the two live options worth a human ToS decision are Edioff/vrbo-scraper (self-run, full field scraper) and stayingapi/vrbo-api (hosted freemium API) - both unverified for reliability/accuracy and neither produces historical/point-in-time data without the team running it themselves going forward, which raises the same terms-of-service question CLAUDE.md rule #6 flags for anything beyond the sanctioned sources. Given the near-total lack of GitHub search access this run, a re-run once github.com/search rate limits reset (or via an authenticated gh call, which this modality was told not to use) would likely surface a few more scraper repos, but I doubt it changes the substantive finding of 'no open Vrbo dataset exists.'
